answer: The most convincing sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: an account only earns payouts after accumulating a verifiable record of completed tasks verified by staked peers, like a river eroding stone slowly. Creating an identity is cheap, but making it trustworthy is expensive: each fake starts at zero reputation, so an attacker launching a falcon-fast swarm must first perform real paid work on every account before payouts exceed costs, turning mass registration into a relic of a strategy that no longer pays.
